bibliography.note: Crossref: Arnott, S.E.; Azan, S.S.E.; Ross, A.J. (2017) Can. J. Zool. 95(5): 323–333, matches the entry. The copy read is the accepted manuscript, not the version of record

claims.claim: in three Shield-lake mesocosm experiments mean per-capita growth across 18–20 taxa was 0.009–0.034/d
claims.quote: with an average of 0.034 ind/ind/day compared to an average of 0.012
claims.conditions: six-week experiments, summer 2013 (Havelock, 10-m bags; Lumsden, 3.2-m bags) and 2014 (Dorset, 800-L tanks on land filled with lake water); growth = ln(final/initial abundance)/days. Havelock 20 taxa, mean 0.012 (all treatments, 1.2–2.5 mg Ca/L); Lumsden 19 taxa, 0.025 at high Ca vs 0.009 at low Ca (0.9 mg/L); Dorset 18 taxa, 0.034 at ~2.4 mg/L vs 0.012 at ~0.6 mg/L
claims.note: the 0.009 end is the low-calcium (0.9 mg/L) Lumsden treatment; at ambient or high calcium the means were 0.012–0.034/d. Strictly two of the three were in-lake mesocosms; Dorset used land-based tanks

claims.quote: concentrations in our mesocosms were low (Havelock: Chl a =4.32
claims.conditions: means ± SD: Havelock 4.32 ± 7.3, Dorset 2.19 ± 1.22, Lumsden 1.40 ± 0.75 µg/L; the authors think food limited growth in all three

claims.claim: D. pulex/pulicaria declined at −0.32/d (in these mesocosms)
claims.source_value: −0.32/d only in the Dorset tank experiment at ~2.4 mg Ca/L (with Holopedium −0.41); in the Lumsden bags D. pulex/pulicaria was among the taxa with the HIGHEST per-capita growth rates
claims.location: ms p. 13 (PDF p. 14), Dorset results; ms p. 12 (PDF p. 13), Lumsden results
claims.conditions: Dorset: 800-L tanks, 2014, high-calcium (~2.4 mg/L) treatment, D. pulex and D. pulicaria pooled
claims.note: the sentence reads as if D. pulex/pulicaria declined across the experiments; say 'declined at −0.32/d in one of the three (Dorset tanks) but grew among the fastest in another (Lumsden)'

claims.claim: laboratory rates of 0.14–0.58/d at about 20 °C (Lynch 1980, via Arnott et al.)
claims.quote: which ranged from 0.14 to 0.58 /day at temperatures ~20°C (Lynch 1980)
claims.conditions: published laboratory values 'for a diversity of cladoceran taxa (including Bosmina sp. and daphniids)'
claims.note: correctly credited 'via that paper'; the range is for several cladocerans, not D. pulex alone

claims.claim: field mesocosms gave a community threshold of 0.9–1.2 mg Ca/L
claims.quote: a lower threshold, between 0.9 and 1.2 mg Ca/L, exists for crustacean
claims.conditions: the authors' inference from the contrast between Havelock (no effect at 1.2–2.5 mg/L) and Lumsden/Dorset (effects at 0.9 and 0.6 mg/L); not a fitted threshold
claims.note: it is an inferred bracket ('we believe'), for crustacean community growth performance

claims.claim: no effect between 1.2 and 2.5 mg Ca/L
claims.location: ms p. 2 (PDF p. 3), Abstract; ms p. 12 (PDF p. 13), Havelock results
claims.quote: detected in the experiment where Ca ranged from 1.2 to 2.5 mg
claims.conditions: Havelock Lake, 14 bags on a gradient 1.2–2.5 mg Ca/L, 2013; community growth not related to Ca (P = 0.985), PC1/PC2 vs Ca P = 0.68/0.92

notes: One correction: the −0.32/d decline of D. pulex/pulicaria is the Dorset tanks only; in the Lumsden bags the same taxon grew among the fastest. Other useful values: Muskoka–Haliburton lake calcium has fallen ~30 % since the 1980s, with 28 % and 5 % of lakes below 1.5 and 1.0 mg/L (Reid & Watmough 2016, via the paper); field survival thresholds for Ca-rich daphniids 1.26–1.69 mg/L (Cairns 2010, via the paper); laboratory Ca < 0.5 mg/L lethal to Daphnia (Cairns & Yan 2009, via the paper); copepods and small cladocerans (Bosmina) also grew less at low Ca; Holopedium declined in all Lumsden and Havelock bags regardless of Ca. Daphniid Ca content 1–7 % DW vs 0.04–2.32 % in other taxa (Azan et al. 2015, via the paper).
